public_domain_references.kjv: O Jerusalem, wash thine heart from wickedness, that thou mayest be saved. How long shall thy vain thoughts lodge within thee?
public_domain_references.brenton: Cleanse thine heart from wickedness, O Jerusalem, that thou mayest be saved: how long will thy grievous thoughts be within thee?

pob.text: Like watchmen of a field[a], they are against her all around, because she has rebelled against me, declares Yahweh.

spob.text: Like guards around a field, they stand against her on every side because she has rebelled against me, declares Yahweh.

public_domain_references.web: As keepers of a field, they are against her all around, because she has been rebellious against me,’” says Yahweh.

public_domain_references.kjv: As keepers of a field, are they against her round about; because she hath been rebellious against me, saith the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: As keepers of a field, they have surrounded her; because thou, saith the Lord, hast neglected me.

pob.text: Your way and your deeds have brought these things upon you. This is your evil[a]—how bitter it is! For it has reached your heart.

spob.text: The way you have lived and what you have done have brought these things on you. This is your evil[a]—how bitter it is! It has reached your heart.

public_domain_references.bsb: “Your ways and deeds have brought this upon you. This is your punishment; how bitter it is, because it pierces to the heart!”
public_domain_references.web: “Your way and your doings have brought these things to you. This is your wickedness, for it is bitter, for it reaches to your heart.”

public_domain_references.kjv: Thy way and thy doings have procured these [things] unto thee; this [is] thy wickedness, because it is bitter, because it reacheth unto thine heart.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thy ways and thy devices have brought these things upon thee; this is thy wickedness, for [it is] bitter, for it has reached to thy heart.

pob.text: My inward parts[a], my inward parts! I writhe in pain! O walls of my heart! My heart pounds within me; I cannot keep silent, for you, my soul, have heard the sound of the trumpet[c][b], the battle cry.

spob.text: My insides, my insides! I writhe in pain! O walls of my heart![a] My heart pounds within me. I cannot keep silent, for you, my soul, have heard the trumpet sound and the battle cry.[b]

public_domain_references.web: My anguish, my anguish! I am pained at my very heart! My heart trembles within me. I can’t hold my peace, because you have heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
public_domain_references.asv: My anguish, my anguish! I am pained at my very heart; my heart is disquieted in me; I cannot hold my peace; because thou hast heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ My bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart; my heart maketh a noise in me; I cannot hold my peace, because thou hast heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
public_domain_references.brenton: I am pained in my bowels, my bowels, and the sensitive powers of my heart; my soul is in great commotion, my heart is torn: I will not be silent, for my soul has heard the sound of a trumpet, the cry of war, and of distress: it calls on destruction;

pob.text: Disaster upon disaster is proclaimed[a], for the whole land is devastated. Suddenly my tents are devastated[b], my curtains in a moment.

spob.text: Disaster upon disaster is announced, because the whole land is devastated.[a] Suddenly my tents are devastated; my tent curtains are devastated in a moment.

public_domain_references.bsb: Disaster after disaster is proclaimed, for the whole land is laid waste. My tents are destroyed in an instant, my curtains in a moment.
public_domain_references.web: Destruction on destruction is decreed, for the whole land is laid waste. Suddenly my tents are destroyed, and my curtains gone in a moment.
public_domain_references.asv: Destruction upon destruction is cried; for the whole land is laid waste: suddenly are my tents destroyed, [and] my curtains in a moment.
public_domain_references.kjv: Destruction upon destruction is cried; for the whole land is spoiled: suddenly are my tents spoiled, [and] my curtains in a moment.
public_domain_references.brenton: for all the land is distressed: suddenly [my] tabernacle is distressed, my curtains have been rent asunder.

pob.text: How long must I see the signal flag and hear the sound of the trumpet?[a][b]

spob.text: How much longer must I keep watching the signal flag and listening to the warning trumpet?[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: How long must I see the signal flag and hear the sound of the horn?
public_domain_references.web: How long will I see the standard and hear the sound of the trumpet?
public_domain_references.asv: How long shall I see the standard, and hear the sound of the trumpet?
public_domain_references.kjv: How long shall I see the standard, [and] hear the sound of the trumpet?
public_domain_references.brenton: How long shall I see fugitives, and hear the sound of the trumpet?

pob.text: For my people are foolish; they do not know me. They are foolish children[a], and they have no understanding. They are wise to do evil, but they do not know how to do good.

spob.text: For my people are fools who do not know me. They are children[a] without good sense or understanding. They are wise only when it comes to doing evil; they do not know how to do good.

public_domain_references.web: “For my people are foolish. They don’t know me. They are foolish children, and they have no understanding. They are skillful in doing evil, but they don’t know how to do good.”

public_domain_references.brenton: For the princes of my people have not known me, they are foolish and unwise children: they are wise to do evil, but [how] to do good they have not known.

pob.text: I looked at the earth[a], and behold, it was formless and empty; and at the heavens, and they had no light.

spob.text: I looked at the earth, and there it was—formless and empty.[a] I looked at the heavens, and they had no light.

public_domain_references.bsb: I looked at the earth, and it was formless and void; I looked to the heavens, and they had no light.
public_domain_references.web: I saw the earth and, behold, it was waste and void, and the heavens, and they had no light.
public_domain_references.asv: I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was waste and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.
public_domain_references.kjv: I beheld the earth, and, lo, [it was] without form, and void; and the heavens, and they [had] no light.
public_domain_references.brenton: I looked upon the earth, and, behold, [it was] not; and to the sky, and there was no light in it.

spob.text: I looked at the mountains—and there they were, quaking. All the hills were shaking.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking; all the hills were swaying.
public_domain_references.web: I saw the mountains, and behold, they trembled, and all the hills moved back and forth.
public_domain_references.asv: I beheld the mountains, and, lo, they trembled, and all the hills moved to and fro.
public_domain_references.kjv: I beheld the mountains, and, lo, they trembled, and all the hills moved lightly.
public_domain_references.brenton: I beheld the mountains, and they trembled, and [I saw] all the hills in commotion.

pob.text: I looked[a], and behold, there was no man, and all the birds of the heavens had fled.

spob.text: I looked—no man was there. All the birds of the sky had fled.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: I looked, and no man was left; all the birds of the air had fled.
public_domain_references.web: I saw, and behold, there was no man, and all the birds of the sky had fled.
public_domain_references.asv: I beheld, and, lo, there was no man, and all the birds of the heavens were fled.
public_domain_references.kjv: I beheld, and, lo, [there was] no man, and all the birds of the heavens were fled.
public_domain_references.brenton: I looked, and, behold, there was no man, and all the birds of the sky were scared.

pob.text: I looked[a], and behold, the fruitful land was a wilderness, and all its cities were torn down before Yahweh[b], before his fierce anger.

spob.text: I looked, and there before me was the fertile land[a]—a wilderness. All its cities were torn down before Yahweh, before his fierce anger.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: I looked, and the fruitful land was a desert. All its cities were torn down before the LORD, before His fierce anger.
public_domain_references.web: I saw, and behold, the fruitful field was a wilderness, and all its cities were broken down at the presence of Yahweh, before his fierce anger.
public_domain_references.asv: I beheld, and, lo, the fruitful field was a wilderness, and all the cities thereof were broken down at the presence of Jehovah, [and] before his fierce anger.
public_domain_references.kjv: I beheld, and, lo, the fruitful place [was] a wilderness, and all the cities thereof were broken down at the presence of the LORD, [and] by his fierce anger.
public_domain_references.brenton: I saw, and, behold, Carmel was desert, and all the cities were burnt with fire at the presence of the Lord, and at the presence of his fierce anger they were utterly destroyed.

pob.text: For thus says Yahweh: The whole land will be a desolation[b][a], yet I will not make a full end.

spob.text: For this is what Yahweh says: “The whole land will be devastated,[a] but I will not destroy it completely.”

public_domain_references.asv: For thus saith Jehovah, The whole land shall be a desolation; yet will I not make a full end.
public_domain_references.kjv: For thus hath the LORD said, The whole land shall be desolate; yet will I not make a full end.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thus saith the Lord, The whole land shall be desolate; but I will not make a full end.

pob.text: Because of this the earth will mourn[a], and the heavens above will grow dark, because I have spoken, I have purposed, and I have not relented[c][b], nor will I turn back from it.

spob.text: Because of this, the earth[a] will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark. For I have spoken and made my decision. I have not relented, and I will not turn back from it.

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore the earth will mourn and the heavens above will grow dark. I have spoken, I have planned, and I will not relent or turn back.”
public_domain_references.web: For this the earth will mourn, and the heavens above be black, because I have spoken it. I have planned it, and I have not repented, neither will I turn back from it.”
public_domain_references.asv: For this shall the earth mourn, and the heavens above be black; because I have spoken it, I have purposed it, and I have not repented, neither will I turn back from it.
public_domain_references.kjv: For this shall the earth mourn, and the heavens above be black: because I have spoken [it], I have purposed [it], and will not repent, neither will I turn back from it.
public_domain_references.brenton: For these things let the earth mourn, and let the sky be dark above: for I have spoken, and I will not repent; I have purposed, and I will not turn back from it.

pob.text: At the sound of the horseman and the archer[a], every city flees; they go into the thickets and climb up among the rocks. Every city is abandoned[d][c][b], and no man dwells in them.

spob.text: At the sound of the horseman and the archer,[a] every city empties as its people flee. They hide in the thickets[b] and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned, and no man lives in any of them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Every city flees at the sound of the horseman and archer. They enter the thickets and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned; no inhabitant is left.
public_domain_references.web: Every city flees for the noise of the horsemen and archers. They go into the thickets and climb up on the rocks. Every city is forsaken, and not a man dwells therein.
public_domain_references.asv: Every city fleeth for the noise of the horsemen and bowmen; they go into the thickets, and climb up upon the rocks: every city is forsaken, and not a man dwelleth therein.
public_domain_references.kjv: The whole city shall flee for the noise of the horsemen and bowmen; they shall go into thickets, and climb up upon the rocks: every city [shall be] forsaken, and not a man dwell therein.
public_domain_references.brenton: The whole land has recoiled from the noise of the horseman and the bent bow; they have gone into the caves, and have hidden themselves in the groves, and have gone up upon the rocks: every city was abandoned, no man dwelt in them.

pob.text: And you[a], devastated one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, you beautify yourself in vain. Your lovers despise you[b]; they seek your life.

spob.text: And you, devastated one,[a] what will you do? Even if you dress in scarlet, put on gold jewelry, and make your eyes look larger with dark makeup,[b] all your efforts to make yourself beautiful are useless. Your lovers despise you and seek to kill you.

public_domain_references.bsb: And you, O devastated one, what will you do, though you dress yourself in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with gold jewelry, though you enlarge your eyes with paint? You adorn yourself in vain; your lovers despise you; they want to take your life.
public_domain_references.web: You, when you are made desolate, what will you do? Though you clothe yourself with scarlet, though you deck yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with makeup, you make yourself beautiful in vain. Your lovers despise you. They seek your life.
public_domain_references.asv: And thou, when thou art made desolate, what wilt thou do? Though thou clothest thyself with scarlet, though thou deckest thee with ornaments of gold, though thou enlargest thine eyes with paint, in vain dost thou make thyself fair; [thy] lovers despise thee, they seek thy life.
public_domain_references.kjv: And [when] thou [art] spoiled, what wilt thou do? Though thou clothest thyself with crimson, though thou deckest thee with ornaments of gold, though thou rentest thy face with painting, in vain shalt thou make thyself fair; [thy] lovers will despise thee, they will seek thy life.
public_domain_references.brenton: And what wilt thou do? Though thou clothe thyself with scarlet, and adorn thyself with golden ornaments; though thou adorn thine eyes with stibium, thy beauty [will be] in vain: thy lovers have rejected thee, they seek thy life.

pob.text: For I have heard a sound like a woman in labor[a], distress like one giving birth to her first child— the sound of Daughter Zion gasping for breath, spreading out her hands: “Woe is me[c][b], for my life is faint before killers.”

spob.text: For I have heard a sound like that of a woman in labor, distress like that of a woman giving birth to her first child. It is the sound of Daughter Zion[a], gasping for breath and spreading out her hands: “Woe is me! My life is growing faint before killers.”

public_domain_references.bsb: For I hear a cry like a woman in labor, a cry of anguish like one bearing her first child— the cry of the Daughter of Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands to say, “Woe is me, for my soul faints before the murderers!”
public_domain_references.web: For I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, the anguish as of her who gives birth to her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion, who gasps for breath, who spreads her hands, saying, “Woe is me now! For my soul faints before the murderers.”
public_domain_references.asv: For I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, the anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion, that gaspeth for breath, that spreadeth her hands, [saying], Woe is me now! for my soul fainteth before the murderers.
public_domain_references.kjv: For I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, [and] the anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion, [that] bewaileth herself, [that] spreadeth her hands, [saying], Woe [is] me now! for my soul is wearied because of murderers.
public_domain_references.brenton: For I have heard thy groaning as the voice of a woman in travail, as of her that brings forth her first child; the voice of the daughter of Zion shall fail through weakness, and she shall lose the strength of her hands, [saying], Woe is me! for my soul faints because of the slain.

pob.text: Roam through the streets of Jerusalem[a], and please look and know, and search in her squares, whether you can find a man, whether there is one who does justice, who seeks faithfulness[b], and I will forgive her.

spob.text: Go all through the streets of Jerusalem. Please look carefully and find out what is there. Search her public squares. See whether you can find even one man[a] who acts with justice and seeks faithfulness.[b] Then I will forgive her.

public_domain_references.bsb: “Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem. Look now and take note; search her squares. If you can find a single person, anyone who acts justly, anyone who seeks the truth, then I will forgive the city.
public_domain_references.web: “Run back and forth through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in its wide places, if you can find a man, if there is anyone who does justly, who seeks truth, then I will pardon her.
public_domain_references.asv: Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that doeth justly, that seeketh truth; and I will pardon her.
public_domain_references.kjv: Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be [any] that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it.
public_domain_references.brenton: Run ye about in the streets of Jerusalem, and see, and know, and seek in her broad places, if ye can find [one], if there is any one that does judgment, and seeks faithfulness; and I will pardon them, saith the Lord.

pob.text: And if they say, “As the LORD lives,” even so they swear falsely.

spob.text: Even if they say, “As surely as the LORD lives,” they are still swearing falsely.

public_domain_references.bsb: Although they say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ they are swearing falsely.”
public_domain_references.web: Though they say, ‘As Yahweh lives,’ surely they swear falsely.”
public_domain_references.asv: And though they say, As Jehovah liveth; surely they swear falsely.
public_domain_references.kjv: And though they say, The LORD liveth; surely they swear falsely.
public_domain_references.brenton: The Lord lives, they say; do they not therefore swear falsely?

pob.text: O Yahweh[a], are not your eyes on faithfulness? You struck them, but they did not feel pain; you consumed them, but they refused to accept discipline. They made their faces harder than rock[b]; they refused to return.

spob.text: Yahweh, don’t your eyes look for faithfulness? You struck them, but they felt no pain.[a] You devastated them, yet they refused to accept your correction. They made their faces harder than rock and refused to return to you.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: O LORD, do not Your eyes look for truth? You struck them, but they felt no pain. You finished them off, but they refused to accept discipline. They have made their faces harder than stone and refused to repent.
public_domain_references.web: O Yahweh, don’t your eyes look on truth? You have stricken them, but they were not grieved. You have consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction. They have made their faces harder than a rock. They have refused to return.
public_domain_references.asv: O Jehovah, do not thine eyes look upon truth? thou hast stricken them, but they were not grieved; thou hast consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return.
public_domain_references.kjv: O LORD, [are] not thine eyes upon the truth? thou hast stricken them, but they have not grieved; thou hast consumed them, [but] they have refused to receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return.
public_domain_references.brenton: O Lord, thine eyes are upon faithfulness: thou hast scourged them, but they have not grieved; thou hast consumed them; but they would not receive correction: they have made their faces harder than a rock; and they would not return.

pob.text: But I said[a], “Surely these are only the poor; they are foolish, for they do not know the way of Yahweh, the justice of their God.”

spob.text: But I said, “Surely these are just poor people. They are foolish because they do not know how Yahweh wants them to live or what their God establishes as right.[a]”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I said, “They are only the poor; they have played the fool, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.
public_domain_references.web: Then I said, “Surely these are poor. They are foolish; for they don’t know Yahweh’s way, nor the law of their God.
public_domain_references.asv: Then I said, Surely these are poor; they are foolish; for they know not the way of Jehovah, nor the law of their God:
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore I said, Surely these [are] poor; they are foolish: for they know not the way of the LORD, [nor] the judgment of their God.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then I said, It may be they are poor; for they are weak, for they know not the way of the Lord, or the judgment of God.

pob.text: I will go to the great men and speak to them[a], for they know the way of Yahweh, the justice of their God. But they too, together, have broken the yoke; they have torn off the bonds.

spob.text: I will go and speak to the prominent men. They know Yahweh’s way and the justice of their God.[a] Yet together they have broken the yoke and torn off the bonds.

public_domain_references.bsb: I will go to the powerful and speak to them. Surely they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.” But they too, with one accord, had broken the yoke and torn off the chains.
public_domain_references.web: I will go to the great men and will speak to them, for they know the way of Yahweh, and the law of their God.” But these with one accord have broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.
public_domain_references.asv: I will get me unto the great men, and will speak unto them; for they know the way of Jehovah, and the law of their God. But these with one accord have broken the yoke, and burst the bonds.
public_domain_references.kjv: I will get me unto the great men, and will speak unto them; for they have known the way of the LORD, [and] the judgment of their God: but these have altogether broken the yoke, [and] burst the bonds.
public_domain_references.brenton: I will go to the rich men, and will speak to them; for they have known the way of the Lord, and the judgment of God: but, behold, with one consent they have broken the yoke, they have burst the bonds.

pob.text: Therefore a lion from the forest strikes them down[a]; a wolf of the deserts devastates them; a leopard keeps watch over their cities. Everyone who goes out from them will be torn apart, because their transgressions are many[b]; their apostasies have grown strong.

spob.text: Therefore, a lion from the forest strikes them down. A wolf from the desert plains[a] devastates them. A leopard lies in wait near their cities. Anyone who goes out of their cities will be torn apart, because their acts of rebellion are many and their apostasies[b] have intensified.

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them down, a wolf from the desert will ravage them. pob.text: Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your soul loathe Zion? Why have you struck us so that there is no healing for us? We hoped for peace[a], but there was no good, and for a time of healing, but behold[b], terror.

pob.text: Are there any among the idols of the nations that bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Is it not you[a], O Yahweh our God? And we wait for you[c][b], for you have made all these things.

pob.text: Woe to me[a], my mother, because you bore me, a man of strife and a man of contention to all the land. I have not lent, nor have they lent to me[b], yet every one of them curses me.

public_domain_references.web: Will the snow of Lebanon fail from the rock of the field? Will the cold waters that flow down from afar be dried up?
public_domain_references.asv: Shall the snow of Lebanon fail from the rock of the field? [or] shall the cold waters that flow down from afar be dried up?

public_domain_references.brenton: Will fertilising streams fail [to flow] from a rock, or snow [fail] from Libanus? will water violently impelled by the wind turn aside?

pob.text: For my people have forgotten me[a]; they burn incense to emptiness. They have stumbled in their ways, in the ancient paths, to walk on side roads[d][c][b], on a road not built up.

pob.text: Then they said[a], “Come, let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise man, nor word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not pay attention to any of his words.”

pob.text: Pay attention to me[a], O Yahweh, and hear the voice of my adversaries.

public_domain_references.asv: Shall evil be recompensed for good? for they have digged a pit for my soul. Remember how I stood before thee to speak good for them, to turn away thy wrath from them.

pob.text: Therefore give their children over to famine[a], and hand them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives become bereaved and widowed, and let their men be slain by death[c][b], their young men struck down by the sword in battle.

pob.text: Let a cry be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring a raiding band upon them[b][a], for they have dug a pit to capture me and hidden traps for my feet.

spob.text: When you suddenly bring a band of raiders against them, let a cry of distress be heard from their houses, for they have dug a pit to capture me and hidden traps for my feet.

pob.text: But you[a], O Yahweh, know all their counsel against me for death. Do not cover over their iniquity, and do not blot out their sin from before you. Let them be made to stumble before you; in the time of your anger[c][b], act against them.

spob.text: But you, Yahweh, know every plan they have made to kill me. Do not cover over[a] their wrongdoing, and do not blot out their sin from your sight. Make them stumble before you. When the time of your anger comes, act against them.

public_domain_references.bsb: But You, O LORD, know all their deadly plots against me. Do not wipe out their guilt or blot out their sin from Your sight. Let them be overthrown before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger.

public_domain_references.kjv: Yet, LORD, thou knowest all their counsel against me to slay [me:] forgive not their iniquity, neither blot out their sin from thy sight, but let them be overthrown before thee; deal [thus] with them in the time of thine anger.

“The LORD will roar from high above.

He will roar with all his might against his pasture.
Like workers treading grapes, he will answer with a shout
against everyone who lives on the earth.”

pob.text: You who dwell by many waters[a], rich in treasures, your end has come[b], the measure of your greed.

pob.text: Yahweh of hosts has sworn by himself: Surely I will fill you with men[a], like locusts[c][b], and they will raise over you a shout.

pob.text: He made the earth by his power[a], he established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.

public_domain_references.kjv: He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heaven by his understanding.

pob.text: At the sound of his voice, a multitude of waters is in the heavens; he makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth; he makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the wind from his storehouses.

spob.text: When his voice sounds, there is a vast amount of water in the heavens. He raises clouds[a] from the farthest reaches of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings the wind out of his storehouses.

public_domain_references.brenton: [As for] the word which thou hast spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not hearken to thee.

pob.text: Every man is made brutish[a], without knowledge; every metalworker is put to shame by his idol, for his cast image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

spob.text: Every man becomes senseless and has no knowledge. Every metalworker is put to shame by his idol, because his cast image is a lie. There is no breath[a] in these idols.

pob.text: They are vanity[a], a work of delusion[b]; at the time of their punishment they will perish.

public_domain_references.bsb: They are worthless, a work to be mocked. In the time of their punishment they will perish.

public_domain_references.kjv: They [are] vanity, the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish.
public_domain_references.brenton: But since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, we have all been brought low, and have been consumed by sword and by famine.

pob.text: Not like these is the Portion of Jacob[a], for he is the one who formed everything, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance[c][b]; Yahweh of Armies is his name.

spob.text: The God who is Jacob’s Portion[a] is nothing like these idols. He formed everything, and Israel is the people who belong to him as his inheritance.[b] His name is Yahweh of Armies.

public_domain_references.brenton: And whereas we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured drink-offerings to her, did we make cakes to her, and pour drink-offerings to her, without our husbands?

pob.text: You are my war club[a], my weapon of battle; with you I shatter nations[b], and with you I destroy kingdoms.

pob.text: And I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all their evil that they have done in Zion before your eyes[a], declares Yahweh.

pob.text: Raise a banner in the land[a]; blow a trumpet among the nations. Consecrate nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a marshal against her[d][c][b]; bring up horses like bristling locusts.

spob.text: Raise a signal banner in the land, and sound the trumpet among the nations. Set nations apart for war against her.[a] Call the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz to attack her. Appoint a military officer against her.[b] Bring the horses forward like bristling locusts.[c]

spob.text: Prepare the nations for holy war against her—the kings of Media, her governors and all her subordinate officials, and every country under his rule.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Prepare the nations for battle against her— the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the lands they rule.

pob.text: “My violence and my flesh be upon Babylon,” says the inhabitant of Zion[b][a]. “And my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,” says Jerusalem.

pob.text: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king[a], and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem[b]. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

pob.text: And he did what was evil in the eyes of Yahweh[a], according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

spob.text: He did what was evil in Yahweh’s eyes, following the whole pattern of Jehoiakim’s conduct.

public_domain_references.kjv: And he did [that which was] evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

pob.text: For because of the anger of Yahweh it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah[a], until he cast them out from before his face[b]; and Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

spob.text: Because Yahweh was angry, this happened in Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them away from his presence.[a] Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

pob.text: And in the ninth year of his reign[a], in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came—he and all his army—against Jerusalem[b], and they encamped against it and built a siege wall around it.

pob.text: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

pob.text: In the fourth month[a], on the ninth day of the month, the famine became severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

pob.text: Then the city was breached[a], and all the men of war fled and went out of the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden, while the Chaldeans were all around the city[c][b]; and they went by way of the Arabah.

pob.text: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho[b][a], and all his army was scattered from him.

pob.text: They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath[a], and he passed sentence on him.

spob.text: They captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. There the king of Babylon passed sentence on him.

pob.text: Then the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes[a], and he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.

spob.text: Then the king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons while Zedekiah watched. He also slaughtered all Judah’s officials at Riblah.

public_domain_references.kjv: And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah.

pob.text: Then he blinded Zedekiah’s eyes[a], bound him with bronze shackles, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in the house of custody until the day of his death.

spob.text: The king of Babylon blinded Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him in bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon. There he put Zedekiah in prison[a] until the day of his death.

pob.text: In the fifth month[a], on the tenth day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon[c][b], came to Jerusalem.

pob.text: And all the walls around Jerusalem were broken down by all the army of the Chaldeans that was with the captain of the guard[a][b].

pob.text: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest[a], and Zephaniah the second priest[c][b], and the three keepers of the threshold.

spob.text: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest[a], Zephaniah the second-ranking priest[b], and the three guards who kept watch at the threshold.

public_domain_references.bsb: The captain of the guard also took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers.
public_domain_references.web: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold,

public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:
public_domain_references.brenton: And the captain of the guard took the chief priest, and the second priest, and those that kept the way;

pob.text: And from the city he took one court official who had been appointed over the men of war[a], and seven men from those who saw the king’s face, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found within the city.

spob.text: He also took these people from the city: one court official[a] who was in charge of the soldiers; seven men from the king’s court who had direct access to him and were found in the city; the army commander’s secretary, who called the people of the country into military service; and sixty men from the people of the country who were found in the city.

public_domain_references.bsb: Of those still in the city, he took a court official who had been appointed over the men of war, as well as seven trusted royal advisers. He also took the scribe of the captain of the army, who had enlisted the people of the land, and sixty men who were found in the city.
public_domain_references.web: and out of the city he took an officer who was set over the men of war; and seven men of those who saw the king’s face, who were found in the city; and the scribe of the captain of the army, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land, who were found in the middle of the city.
public_domain_references.asv: and out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war; and seven men of them that saw the king’s face, that were found in the city; and the scribe of the captain of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city.
public_domain_references.kjv: He took also out of the city an eunuch, which had the charge of the men of war; and seven men of them that were near the king’s person, which were found in the city; and the principal scribe of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city.
public_domain_references.brenton: and one eunuch, who was over the men of war, and seven men of renown, who were in the king's presence, that were found in the city; and the scribe of the forces, who did the part of a scribe to the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land, who were found in the midst of the city.

pob.text: Nebuzaradan[a], the captain of the guard[b], took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

spob.text: Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took these people and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
public_domain_references.web: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
public_domain_references.asv: And Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
public_domain_references.kjv: So Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Nabuzardan the captain of the king's guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Deblatha.

pob.text: And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath[a]. So Judah was taken into exile from its land.

spob.text: At Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. Then Judah was forced into exile from its land.

public_domain_references.bsb: There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land.
public_domain_references.web: The king of Babylon struck them, and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.
public_domain_references.asv: And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the king of Babylon smote them in Deblatha, in the land of Æmath.

pob.text: These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year[b][a], 3,023 Judeans.

spob.text: In the seventh year, Nebuchadnezzar forced 3,023 Judeans[a] into exile.

public_domain_references.bsb: These are the people Nebuchadnezzar carried away: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;

public_domain_references.asv: This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty;
public_domain_references.kjv: This [is] the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty:

pob.text: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar[a], from Jerusalem, 832 persons.

spob.text: In Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, 832 people were taken from Jerusalem.

public_domain_references.bsb: in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;
public_domain_references.web: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty-two persons;

pob.text: In the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar[a], Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away 745 Judeans[c][b]. All the persons were 4,600.

spob.text: In the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took 745 Judeans into exile. The total number taken into exile in all these deportations was 4,600.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: in Nebuchadnezzar’s twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried away 745 Jews. So in all, 4,600 people were taken away.
public_domain_references.web: in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty-five people. All the people numbered four thousand six hundred.
public_domain_references.asv: in the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred.
public_domain_references.kjv: In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons [were] four thousand and six hundred.

pob.text: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah[a], in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign[b], lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out from the prison.

spob.text: In the thirty-seventh year that Jehoiachin king of Judah was in exile, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, King Evil-merodach of Babylon[a] lifted up Jehoiachin’s head—showing him favor—and brought him out of prison. This was the first year of Evil-merodach’s reign.

public_domain_references.bsb: On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the first year of the reign of Evil-merodach king of Babylon, he pardoned Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.
public_domain_references.web: In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and released him from prison.
public_domain_references.asv: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the [first] year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison;
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth [day] of the month, [that] Evil-merodach king of Babylon in the [first] year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison,
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year after that Joakim king of Juda had been carried away captive, in the twelfth month, on the four and twentieth [day] of the month, [that] Ulæmadachar king of Babylon, in the year in which he began to reign, raised the head of Joakim king of Juda, and shaved him, and brought him out of the house where he was kept,

pob.text: He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon[a].

spob.text: He spoke kindly to him and placed his throne higher than the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

public_domain_references.bsb: And he spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

pob.text: And he changed out of his prison clothes and ate bread before him continually all the days of his life[a][b].

spob.text: He changed out of his prison clothes and regularly ate his meals in the king’s presence for the rest of his life.

public_domain_references.bsb: So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he dined regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
public_domain_references.web: and changed his prison garments. Jehoiachin ate bread before him continually all the days of his life.
public_domain_references.asv: and changed his prison garments. And [Jehoiachin] did eat bread before him continually all the days of his life:

public_domain_references.brenton: and changed his prison garments: and he ate bread continually before him all the days that he lived.

pob.text: And his allowance[a], a continual allowance, was given to him from the king of Babylon, a daily portion day by day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

spob.text: The king of Babylon gave him a regular allowance—a portion for each day—for the rest of his life, until the day he died.
